stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on May 8th.
stocks.news: Tech led Friday's tape with NASDAQ +1.71%. Two threads worth watching under the price. Michael Burry, the Big Short investor who's been shorting Palantir (PLTR +0.54%) and exited his GameStop stake, just called this market the late innings of the 1999-2000 bubble. Take Burry as a sentiment read, not a trade signal, but he's worth tracking. The other thread is the workplace cost side of AI. TTEC (TTEC -11.44%) suspended its U.S. 401k match through 2026 to free cash for AI investments. Deloitte and Zoom have pulled back parental leave and pension benefits this year. AI is no longer a future P&L line item, it's actively redirecting compensation budgets. Toyota (TM -0.78%) missed the quarter and cut full-year guidance, blaming U.S. tariffs and Chinese rivals, even as it commits $10B to U.S. plant investment over the next decade.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET May 10th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year barely moved at 4.39%, gold cooled to $4,697 (-0.70%), and WTI ripped to $99.65 (+4.43%) intraday. Brent moved in lockstep at $105.03 (+3.69%). That's the kind of one-day energy jump that shows up in inflation prints two cycles out, worth watching.

April payrolls came in at 115,000, double the consensus, with unemployment held at 4.3%. Strong on the surface. The fine print: information services shed another 13,000 jobs and is now down 342,000 since November 2022. The AI displacement story now has a number on it.

University of Michigan consumer sentiment just hit a fresh record low in April, breaking the record set in March. One in three Americans blamed gas, one in three blamed tariffs. With gas already at $4.56 nationally and crude up another 4% this morning, the sentiment ceiling stays capped through summer.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on May 10th.
crypto.commentary: Bitcoin slipped to $81,190 (-1.21%), ETH at $2,345 (-1.00%), XRP at $1.45 (-1.27%). The bigger crypto story is in flows, not price. Roundhill's Memory ETF, the AI memory chip ETF, pulled in $1.1B Thursday alone, the kind of inflow only Bitcoin ETFs and three other funds in history have ever clocked that fast. $5B in since April 2. The capital chasing AI now has a measurable ETF footprint. Separately, the Revolut app glitched Friday and briefly priced Bitcoin at 2 cents for a few seconds. Some of its 70 million users claim they got fills at that price. A small group claiming Lambo-for-pocket-change is going to be a multi-week story.

real_estate.homebuilder: Builders Cut New-Home Prices To 5-Year Low As 9-In-10 Voters Call Buying Harder Than Ever
real_estate.commentary:
Two national signals worth carrying into Bay Area conversations this week. New home prices fell to a five-year low in March, with 682,000 new homes sold and many now getting price cuts. That's the new-construction segment caving on price, which historically pressures resale within six to nine months. Buyers watching the builder discount tape have a window before resale repositions.

The NAR voter poll: nine in ten say buying a home is harder now than ever. Only 17% think now is a good time to buy, down from 69% in 2013. Just 9% think federal housing policy is helping. That's the consumer mindset framing every showing. The qualified buyer still in the hunt has internalized both the rate environment and the affordability math, they're not waiting for a print.

Rates eased a fraction: 30-year 6.42% (-2 bps), 15-year 5.99% (-1 bp). Holding near 6.4% gives buyers time to underwrite a known number.

For listing agents: the national builder-discount story matters more than usual this week. Buyers comparing your resale listing to a builder cutting $25-50K three exits away need a counter-narrative. Get the comp comparison and the location/school/neighborhood pitch ready before the buyer brings it up.
